source.version_note: Behavioral Sciences 16(10), 1829, published 6 October 2026; received 2 July, revised 17 September and accepted 28 September 2026. September 2025 is the literature-search cutoff, not this article’s publication date.
source.verification_method: All seventeen supplied pages, four figures, nine tables and bibliography read. Search strings and complete PRISMA diagram were visually inspected. Publisher/Crossref verify identity and publication date. Selected primary Knop methods and Blötner abstract/opening paragraphs were read for targeted classification/definition checks; neither receives an independent full-paper reading claim. No private coding matrix or author contact.

citation.title: Rethinking Cognitive Bias in Human–AI Cognitive Systems: A Structured Conceptual Mapping Review

reading.source_scope_note: A structured conceptual map of ten heterogeneous review-level publications uses a bounded September 2025 database search. Its counts describe attention within the retrieved corpus, not independent behavioral replications, population prevalence, causal effects or validated mitigation effectiveness.
access_limits: All main pages, nine tables and four figures read, including image-only search queries and flowchart. The manuscript states that additional extraction files are internal and available on request; no public archive was supplied and no request was made.

The ten included review articles and their primary-study overlap were not independently read and recoded for this review. Their appearance in the bibliography does not earn separate full-paper or behavioral replication credit.

Only selected Knop 2022 methods and the Blötner 2025 abstract plus first two body paragraphs were read. A complete XML was locally retrieved to extract those sections, but the remainder was not treated as read. No data, model code or intervention results reproduced.

Kahneman, Hutchins, Hollnagel/Woods and the original historical jingle/jangle sources were cited by these papers, not independently read as complete books here. No current law or clinical recommendation is established by the mapping.

study.design: Conceptual mapping of review-level publications, intentionally including narrative, conceptual, literature, scoping/systematic and interdisciplinary approaches in eligibility. The authors explicitly distinguish this method from an umbrella review, effect-size synthesis or evidence hierarchy. PRISMA supplies reporting items rather than automatically determining review type.
study.search: Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed searched in September 2025, English, intended 2015–2025 window. ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore and much HCI conference literature are omitted and this is explicitly acknowledged. Adjacent terms such as teaming, overreliance and algorithm appreciation/aversion may be underretrieved.
study.search_image: Figure 1 was read visually. Scopus uses publication year greater than 2014 with no displayed upper bound; PubMed displays a 2015-to-3000 date range; Web of Science explicitly uses 2015–2025. Vocabulary and fields differ, including the human-in-the-loop phrase in Scopus but not the displayed other queries. These are visible reproducibility details; actual query histories and execution-date limits were not supplied.
study.flow: 36 Scopus + 33 Web of Science + 14 PubMed records = 83; minus 34 duplicates leaves 49. Nineteen screened exclusions leave 30 reports sought; twelve preliminary retrieval/eligibility removals leave 18 formal full texts. Three criterion-2 plus five criterion-3 exclusions leave ten. Arithmetic reconciles; the twelve removals’ category-specific reasons are explicitly unavailable, not a fabricated zero attrition rate.
study.coding: Two researchers independently screen and code, compare item by item, then resolve by consensus. One repeats screening as an internal check. Original pre-consensus matrices were not retained, preventing agreement-coefficient calculation. Consensus is not a reconstructed kappa, and unavailable records should not be invented.
study.two_stages: First-order coding retains source labels; second-order mapping distinguishes theoretical frameworks, cognitive processes, relational states, interaction behaviors, proximal outcomes and longitudinal capability changes. The jingle/jangle distinction is used to avoid conflating equivalent labels or counting synonyms as independent constructs.
study.corpus: Ten included publications date from 2020 through September 2025: 1, 1, 2, 0, 2, 4 across 2020–2025. The figure plots years in descending order. These are selected-review counts with a partial final year, not annual mentions of behaviors or evidence that research accelerated.
study.composition: Six healthcare, two multi-domain, one economic and one conceptual/systemic review. Mapped review types are six narrative/conceptual, one non-systematic literature, two mini/special and one interdisciplinary experimental review. These are interpretive categories within the selected corpus, not a census of all reviews or a quality ranking.
study.levels: Human/interaction level is coded in six reviews, algorithmic level in three, data level in one and unspecified level in two. Categories overlap, so the total of twelve assignments is not an arithmetic error. A single data-level code cannot establish rarity or negligible harm of dataset bias.
study.roles: AI support appears in seven, recommendation in two and automation as a concern in four; these role codes overlap. Absence of complete replacement/delegation in this corpus is not proof that such systems or research do not exist. Stated human final responsibility is not a verified universal legal allocation.
study.constructs: Trust appears in five reviews. Table 8 separately lists overreliance under mechanism and outcome, with different contributing reviews; these rows are not independent causal replications or automatically identical constructs. Reduced oversight concerns checking, vigilance concerns monitoring, and acceptance concerns acting on an output. Deskilling requires a longitudinal competence change.
study.mitigation: Human-in-the-loop, explanation, literacy, governance and data practices are mainly recommendations in this corpus, not pooled effectiveness evidence. The authors explicitly cite empirical cognitive-forcing work outside the included set and warn against declaring that no interventions have been tested. Recommendation presence, efficacy, costs and boundary conditions must remain distinct.
study.coupled_systems: Distributed cognition, joint cognitive systems and extended-mind ideas are a sensitizing lens. Emergent human–AI bias is proposed for future testing, not established by ten reviews. Similar observable errors can have different human, interface, model, data and organizational causes.
study.diversity: Cognitive diversity, sensory and age-related needs, digital literacy and accommodations are proposed research/design priorities because the retrieved corpus did not systematically represent them. They are not measured subgroup effects or grounds for ranking people’s rights or competence.
study.primary_checks: A suspected error about Knop’s review type was not supported: its own Methods explicitly calls the work a narrative review. Its use of PRISMA and structured searching does not alone make the mapping’s non-systematic designation false. Preserve this disconfirming check rather than manufacture a source correction.

summary: Add the two complementary concept-naming fallacies, jingle and jangle, with explicit measurement and equivalence boundaries. Strengthen existing automation, deskilling and mental-model records using the source’s distinctions. Keep selected-review counts, conceptual proposals and tested effects separate; no new annual mention totals are inferred.

findings.definition: Treating distinct constructs or measures as equivalent because they share a name.
findings.novelty_rationale: Shared-name equivalence error differs from applying a global label to a person, lexical entrainment or overlooking a diagnosis. The paper explicitly contrasts identical labels denoting different constructs with differently named similar phenomena.
findings.evidence_scope: Conceptual-methodological distinction used to separate source labels, constructs and measurement levels. A targeted primary psychometric definition check confirms the conventional name, not a new human–AI experiment or prevalence estimate.
findings.boundary: A shared name is not sufficient evidence of common content, measurement or mechanism. Conversely, observed differences between scales can arise from noise, contexts or methods. Establish relevant conceptual and empirical differences before declaring a fallacy; this paper does not demonstrate that a model commits it.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual construct-validity distinction in a review; proposed AI information-integration analogue not empirically tested here
findings.ai_proposal: When merging evidence under the same term, compare definitions, measurements, population and causal role. Preserve qualified senses where one label refers to different constructs rather than transferring findings solely by name.

findings.definition: Treating equivalent constructs or measures as distinct because they have different names.
findings.novelty_rationale: Different-name distinction error is the complement of the shared-name jingle error, not a synonym for it. It directly concerns redundant concept creation rather than global labeling, diagnostic overshadowing or adopting another speaker’s vocabulary.

evidence.quote: different labels may denote similar phenomena

findings.evidence_scope: The mapping flags differently named overlapping phenomena and preserves source labels separately from interpretive groupings. The exact fallacy name and equivalence requirement were checked against a primary psychometric definition; similar phenomena alone do not establish identity.
findings.boundary: Related, highly correlated or neighboring constructs need not be equivalent. Similar wording alone is insufficient to merge them, and different measurements can capture meaningful distinctions. Retain parent/subtype, operationalization and context relations when they add defensible information.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual construct-validity distinction; no measured model-specific redundancy error or prevalence estimate
findings.ai_proposal: Before adding a new ontology term, compare its definition, mechanism and measurement with existing entries. Use a synonym only when equivalence is justified; otherwise retain a meaningful subtype or related construct and document the distinction.

findings.definition: Trusting a tool result or a prior step because a machine produced it, without verifying the load-bearing part.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use this bounded conceptual review to clarify the existing construct and evidence level, not to create a duplicate label or claim another primary experiment.

evidence.quote: automation bias, algorithmic bias, data bias

findings.evidence_scope: The mapping distinguishes human reliance and uncritical acceptance from statistical dataset/model bias. Several mechanisms can produce similar errors; review-level mentions do not identify which mechanism caused an individual decision.
findings.boundary: Reliance can be warranted by reliable evidence. Neither human presence, explanation nor a recommendation to check outputs guarantees a calibrated response. This conceptual map adds no independent experimental effect or prevalence estimate.

findings.definition: Dropping its own checking of a tool's output or a subprocess once it assumes the automation is reliable, letting errors through.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use this bounded conceptual review to clarify the existing construct and evidence level, not to create a duplicate label or claim another primary experiment.

evidence.quote: reduced critical oversight, reduced vigilance, and uncritical acceptance

findings.evidence_scope: Verification behavior, sustained monitoring and accepting an output are related but not identical. The source distinguishes them at the conceptual mapping stage rather than treating all reduced checking as one measured cause.
findings.boundary: Lower checking alone does not establish unwarranted complacency without a task-relevant standard, reliability and available attention. No longitudinal monitoring experiment or tested safeguard is supplied by this review.

findings.definition: Loss or weakening of previously acquired skills through reduced independent use or practice.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use this bounded conceptual review to clarify the existing construct and evidence level, not to create a duplicate label or claim another primary experiment.

evidence.quote: deskilling as a longitudinal capability outcome

findings.evidence_scope: Deskilling is classified as a longitudinal capability outcome rather than an immediate error, trust state or one-time act of delegation. Only one included review receives that label in this coding scheme.
findings.boundary: A review mentioning skill loss is not evidence that every AI user loses competence. Demonstrate a previously acquired skill and its retained unaided performance over time, considering practice, task and selection differences.

findings.definition: Constructing or using an internal representation of a situation or system to predict its behavior and guide inference or action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Use this bounded conceptual review to clarify the existing construct and evidence level, not to create a duplicate label or claim another primary experiment.
findings.evidence_scope: The selected literature includes users’ understanding or misunderstanding of AI capabilities. The proposed coupled-systems lens treats models of capabilities as potentially related to interface, expectations and task choices, not as identical to trust.
findings.boundary: A stated expectation is not a complete internal model or proof of consciousness. The review proposes relationships without measuring individual model accuracy or establishing a causal path to reliance.

source_identity_checks.scope: Selected abstract and Methods only, not a complete independent review. Methods expressly identifies a narrative review. PRISMA usage does not justify recategorizing it as systematic. This check refutes the initially considered classification-error hypothesis.

source_identity_checks.title: Extending Lawson and Robins’ (2021) guideline for the evaluation of jingle and jangle fallacies
source_identity_checks.author: Christian Blötner
source_identity_checks.scope: Abstract and first two body paragraphs read; remaining XML not read. Confirms which error is jingle versus jangle and cautions that closely related sibling constructs need not be identical. Definition check only, no separate full-paper or experimental credit.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: PDF 4, Figure 1 and stated search window
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The displayed Scopus query has only a lower year bound and PubMed displays an upper year of 3000, while the text states 2015–2025. Web of Science explicitly bounds both years. September 2025 execution may explain practical coverage, but query histories were not supplied. Report this precision limit without claiming the corpus necessarily includes ineligible records.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: PDF 5, twelve preliminary removals and coding agreement
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The authors explicitly state that category-specific reasons and pre-consensus matrices were not retained. Flow totals reconcile, but exclusion reasons and inter-rater agreement cannot be independently reconstructed. Do not invent a kappa or claim that no screening process occurred.

The statement that patterns are likely more robust in professional contexts is an inference from corpus concentration. Without formal quality appraisal or cross-domain effect comparison, more attention to a domain is not demonstrated empirical robustness.

The prose calls auditability-related practices in Arora continuous evaluation/monitoring, while Table 9 groups them under interpretability/auditability/clinician understanding. With internal coding files unavailable, do not treat those as separately counted or validated interventions.

methodological_limits: Review articles are the unit of analysis, not people, experiments or independent evidence units. Their overlapping primary sources were not quantified; counts must not be summed as behavioral replications.

Restricted databases, English-only selection, review-level eligibility, search vocabulary and a September 2025 cutoff constrain coverage. The source explicitly disclaims an exhaustive account; a rare code is not a rare real-world problem.

No formal quality appraisal, quantitative effect synthesis, causal analysis or mitigation meta-analysis was conducted. The authors openly disclose these boundaries; absence from this map is not absence of primary evidence.

Heuristics can be useful. Cognitive bias relative to a judgment standard, statistical data/model bias and unjust discrimination are related but non-interchangeable. Ethical wrongness is not established by a statistical departure alone.

Conceptual frameworks, processes, relational trust, behaviors, immediate outcomes and longitudinal skill changes need different evidence. The two naming fallacies do not justify indiscriminate merging of similar constructs.

The coupled-system and cognitive-diversity proposals are hypotheses or design priorities, not measured emergent mechanisms or validated subgroup effects. Sensory or cognitive differences do not reduce rights or justify unsupported profiling.

The count of four reviews in partial 2025, absence of a 2023 review and healthcare concentration describe only ten selected reviews. They cannot replace the website’s independently scoped annual literature series.

No source author contacted, nonpublic internal file requested, full cited book claimed read, untested mitigation presented as effective or partial primary definition check counted as a complete review.

cross_paper_learning.finding: A collection of conceptual, legal and review-level publications must not be relabeled as an equal number of primary empirical studies. Recommendation presence is distinct from intervention effectiveness.
Source labels for mind, trust and agency can denote different measurements. Source identity and construct boundaries require review rather than name matching.
Different task formats can yield different dimensional summaries without proving that every conceptual framework is false. Mapping similarity is not proof of construct identity.
Agent–task fit, expected performance, delegation and attributed emotional experience are separate constructs. This distinction illustrates why matching labels alone should not merge their evidence.

deferred.term: Coupled human–AI cognition as a newly demonstrated bias
deferred.reason: A theoretical lens and research proposition, not a specific independently measured behavior or empirical system-emergence result.

deferred.term: Standard-user disadvantage as a confirmed subgroup effect
deferred.reason: Explicitly derived as a future research and accommodation priority; no measured subgroup comparison or causal estimate.

deferred.term: Reduced oversight, reduced vigilance and uncritical acceptance as three automatic new rows
deferred.reason: Related but nonidentical processes need operational definitions and direct source evidence. Preserve the distinction within existing checking/reliance records rather than inflate this conceptual map into multiple independent effects.

deferred.term: Sibling constructs as another behavioral row
deferred.reason: A relation between potentially overlapping constructs, not a behavior itself. Use justified synonym, subtype and related-term relations instead.

limitations: Two new naming-error entries. Stable IDs and eleven categories preserved; no forced citation quota, invented annual counts, automatic ethical/harm edges or full-paper Markdown transcription.
